units.translation: 587-88a. If Zeus himself from heaven: he says that Hermes was sent by Zeus as a messenger, bidding him to receive Phrixus, so that he might marry the daughter of Aeetes. But the author of the Aegimius (Hes.
fr. 184 Rz.²) says that he was received willingly because of the fleece. And he says that after the sacrifice, having purified the fleece, he went thus to the house of Aeetes, holding the fleece.
1 add. AF
b. So that of kindly: that Phrixus might meet with a kindly Aeetes.
c. And 'to meet' means 'to enjoy'. P
589. Lest also: the word 'steuto' is to be supplied from the common context. Lm
7 this gloss is assigned to verse 579 in L, transposed by W

594-98a. Apart from him: he said that he would give punishment to the sons of Phrixus apart from himself; for he said that they were bringing evil men upon him, so that they might gain control of his kingdom, as he had also heard from his own father Helios. And that an oracle had been given to Aeetes that he would be destroyed by his own descendants, Herodorus also relates in his Argonautica (31 fr. 9 J.); for this reason he says that he devised the yoking of the bulls.
12 Αἰόλου instead of αὐτοῦ Robert Die griech. Heldensage 1921, 766 n. 1
b. Uncared for: being unconcerned about him. Lm (P)
599. That it was necessary for him: it is written 'chreiō min'. Lg
600. He improperly used the dual 'sphōiterēs' for a singular; for he should have said 'heēs', so that it would be 'of his own'.

601-02a. By which even desiring: he has used the imperfect instead of the perfect, and the phrase is transposed and the word 'hōs' is missing. For the order is: wherefore even desiring to sail far - and this too must be understood - he has sent them by the command of their father [after he had spoken]. L
20 pluperfect AF transposition F
22 which are alien to this passage, deleted by W 27, ὥς π. ἐ. φρ. πέπ. αὐτούς F
b. 'By the command of his father' instead of: according to the admonition of Helios. P
603. That there was some fear for him: the word 'he understood' is missing. Lm
605. But in Chalciope's: for an oracle had been given to him that he would be destroyed by his relatives, as Herodorus also relates (see scholium on 594-98a). Lm
610. He kept consoling: he kept calling upon, he kept showing affection. Lm (P)
613. Beyond what is fitting: doing what is not proper. Lm
615. Openly: audible, manifest. Lg (P)
616. It kept lulling: sleep kept stopping her from her griefs. Lm (P)
622. And now he improperly used 'spheteron'; for it is plural used for a singular inclusive. But he should have said 'heon domon'. L
3 supplied by W
625. Not soundly even now the word 'sphōiterous'; for it is dual used for singular. He should therefore have said 'heous'. L
628-29a. Both: both entrusted the judgment to the maiden, having agreed to abide by whatever she might decide. Lm (P)
b. So that she might direct: that she might impose upon their minds. Lm
641. 'Empa' instead of 'empēs'. P
643. Their own: instead of 'heois'. Lg
646. Of a solitary: of a solitary. Sm
649. Back: into her own bedchamber. Lg
